mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate predicts a 20-day S&P 500 forward return increase due to lower discount rates applied to future equity cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate predicts a 60-day S&P 500 forward return increase due to lower discount rates applied to future equity cash flows.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate predicts a 20-day S&P 500 forward return decrease due to higher discount rates applied to future equity cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate predicts a 60-day S&P 500 forward return decrease due to higher discount rates applied to future equity cash flows.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) predicts a 20-day S&P 500 forward return increase due to stronger consumer demand and business confidence.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods of rising employment are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) predicts a 60-day S&P 500 forward return increase due to stronger consumer demand and business confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) predicts a 20-day S&P 500 forward return decrease due to weaker consumer demand and business confidence.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods of rising employment are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in periods of rising employment are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
